wars.outcome: Chronicle tradition only: Hunac Ceel 'conquered Chichen Itza in the 13th century' (Chichen Itza page) / 'defeated the rulers of Chichen Itza' (Mayapan page); archaeology puts Chichen Itza's decline before 1100, so no contest is drawn.

notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no Mayapan row; it is inside Later Mayan City-States 1260-1428 (135,191 km2).
DATES. Start 1221 is the Mayapan page's 'some sources date a revolt ... to 1221' and its '1220s'; the infobox's c. 1020 is the earliest charcoal date of the main pyramid, not a state. End 1441 is the written records; the site's abandonment is tentatively 'around A.D. 1461' by archaeology. The page also puts a Xiu riot against the Cocom 'around A.D. 1420'.
TERRITORY. No page gives provinces, tribute or a frontier. The state of Yucatan is a placeholder for 'much of the northern Yucatan' (soft). The sixteen Yucatecan provinces appear on the Spanish conquest of Yucatan page for 1527-1546 and have no dossiers.
CONTRADICTIONS. The Mayapan page says the Landa account 'founded by Kukulcan' and an alternative colonial chronicle claims an alliance with Chichen Itza and Uxmal that archaeology makes 'less likely'; neither is used. The Cocom retreat to Sotuta and the Cocom-Xiu feud are not on the page opened (Not in the text), so are not entered.
COUNTERPARTS. Xiu (Mani) and Cocom (Sotuta) have no dossiers.
